name: Friday Saturday Sunday
tagline: Rittenhouse tasting menu from Chad and Hanna Williams, with a Michelin star.
description: Chef Chad Williams and Hanna Williams run this Rittenhouse restaurant with a tasting menu downstairs and a cocktail bar. It earned one of Philadelphia's first Michelin stars in November 2025. Book ahead.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly Black-owned restaurants guide (updated Aug 7, 2026), owners Chad and Hanna Williams. Open: Michelin star announced Nov 2025 (Axios) and live reservations page.

name: Honeysuckle
tagline: Omar Tate and Cybille St. Aude-Tate's North Broad restaurant.
description: Chefs Omar Tate and Cybille St. Aude-Tate opened this North Broad Street restaurant in April 2025, cooking dishes rooted in Black American foodways. The Michelin Guide added it as a recommended restaurant in 2025.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Inquirer coverage and Visit Philly 2026 guide. Opened April 2025, Michelin recommended 2025. The earlier Honeysuckle Provisions grocery closed in 2024; this row is the restaurant. Phone and website not confirmed, left null.

name: Down North Pizza
tagline: Detroit-style square pies in Strawberry Mansion, staffed by returning citizens.
description: Muhammad Abdul-Hadi opened this Strawberry Mansion pizza shop to employ formerly incarcerated Philadelphians. The menu is built around Detroit-style square pies, wings and fries. Orders go through Tock, and it is open Thursday to Sunday.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly 2026 guide and PhillyVoice (owner Muhammad Abdul-Hadi). Open: live site with hours and Tock ordering, May 2024 PhillyVoice story. Own site lists ZIP 19139; other sources use 19132, which matches Lehigh Ave, so 19132 used.

name: Amina
tagline: Southern cooking with Nigerian touches, now in Northern Liberties.
description: Felicia Wilson and chef Darryl Harmon serve Southern dishes with West African influences. The restaurant moved from Old City and reopened on Germantown Avenue in Northern Liberties in April 2025.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly 2026 guide. Relocated from Old City to Northern Liberties, reopened April 25, 2025 (PhillyVoice Apr 16, 2025; Philly Mag Apr 22, 2025). Phone and website not confirmed on a first-party page, left null.

name: BlackHen
tagline: Old City BYOB fried chicken spot from the team behind Amina.
description: BlackHen is a BYOB fried chicken restaurant in Old City that opened in April 2024. Felicia Wilson owns it, and chef Darryl Harmon built the menu of fried chicken and Southern sides.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Philadelphia Tribune (June 2024) and Visit Philly 2026 guide. Activity: Philly Mag Nov 2024 and Visit Philly Aug 2026. Owner name differs between sources (Tribune vs. others); description uses Felicia Wilson as in Visit Philly. No first-party site confirmed.

name: Booker's Restaurant & Bar
tagline: Daily brunch and Southern plates on Baltimore Avenue.
description: Booker's is a West Philly restaurant and bar on Baltimore Avenue known for its daily brunch. Tracey and Cheri Syphax took over in 2023 from founder Saba Tedla, who opened it in 2017.

_verified.note: Black-owned per 6abc and Visit Philly 2026 guide (owners Tracey and Cheri Syphax). Activity via Visit Philly Aug 2026. The bookersrestaurant.com domain did not resolve, so website left null.

name: SOUTH Restaurant & Jazz Club
tagline: Southern food and live jazz on North Broad from the Bynum brothers.
description: Robert and Benjamin Bynum run this North Broad Street restaurant and jazz club. The kitchen serves Southern food, and the club books live jazz most nights, with tickets sold separately.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly 2026 guide (Bynum brothers). Open: own site lists October 2026 jazz shows. Phone not captured.

name: Kilimandjaro
tagline: Senegalese and West African cooking from Youma Ba, now on Chestnut Street.
description: Youma Ba has cooked Senegalese and West African dishes in West Philly since 2005. The restaurant reopened at 43rd and Chestnut in September 2024 and is BYOB.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Inquirer (Sept 13, 2024) and Visit Philly 2026 guide. Reopened at new address Sept 12, 2024. Phone and website not confirmed.

name: Ma Lessie's Chicken & Waffles
tagline: Soul food and chicken and waffles inside Reading Terminal Market.
description: Cousins Perry Ison and Stacy McCarthy brought soul food back to Reading Terminal Market in 2021. The stall serves fried chicken and waffles plus Southern sides daily.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Reading Terminal Market and Visit Philly 2026 guide. Open: current RTM merchant page with 2026 holiday hours note. Top-up 2026-10-15: Reading Terminal Market map location A5 from the market's merchant page.

name: Sweet T's Bakery
tagline: Sweet potato pies and cakes from Reading Terminal's first Black-owned bakery.
description: Mark and Tia El run Sweet T's, known for sweet potato pie and baked goods. It started in South Philly in 2014 and opened its Reading Terminal Market stall in 2021, the first Black-owned bakery in the market's history.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Reading Terminal Market and Visit Philly 2026 guide. Open: current RTM merchant listing and Visit Philly Aug 2026. Top-up 2026-10-15: Reading Terminal Market map location C11 from the market's merchant page.

name: Denise's Delicacies
tagline: Longtime North Philly bakery for butter cakes and pound cakes.
description: Denise's Delicacies is a family bakery on North 22nd Street founded by Denise Gause and now run by Keshia Davis and Cynthia Benton. The city spotlighted it in 2026 through its Small Business Catalyst Fund.

_verified.note: Black-owned per City of Philadelphia spotlight (July 23, 2026) and Visit Philly 2026 guide. Activity: 6abc Feb 2026, city July 2026. Founding year varies between sources, left null.

name: Two Locals Brewing Company
tagline: Pennsylvania's first Black-owned brewery, pouring at uCity Square.
description: Brothers Richard and Mengistu Koilor founded Two Locals, Pennsylvania's first Black-owned brewery. Their taproom at uCity Square opened in January 2024.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Technical.ly (2025) and Visit Philly 2026 guide. Taproom opened Jan 31, 2024. Phone not confirmed.

name: Kitchen + Kocktails by Kevin Kelley
tagline: Kevin Kelley's Southern comfort food and cocktails at Broad Street.
description: Kevin Kelley's Kitchen + Kocktails opened its Philadelphia location in the Cambria Hotel in October 2025. The menu is Southern comfort food with a full cocktail list.

_verified.note: Black-owned multi-city brand (Kevin Kelley) per Visit Philly 2026 guide and Inquirer (Oct 16, 2025). Slug includes city because the brand has several locations. Phone and site not captured.

name: Suya Suya West African Grill
tagline: Nigerian suya bowls and skewers near Northern Liberties.
description: Dera Nd-Ezuma serves Nigerian suya, spiced grilled meat, in bowls, wraps and skewers. The original shop is on Fairmount Avenue, with a second in Bala Cynwyd.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly 2026 guide (owner Dera Nd-Ezuma). Activity: SJU Hawk News Sept 24, 2025. Second location at 177 City Ave, Bala Cynwyd. Phone and website not confirmed.

name: Black Dragon Takeout
tagline: Kurt Evans' Black American Chinese takeout in West Philly.
description: Chef Kurt Evans opened Black Dragon in August 2024 to serve Black American Chinese takeout, the kind found in corner shops across Black neighborhoods. Expect wings, lo mein and fried rice.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Inquirer (Aug 29, 2024) and Visit Philly 2026 guide. Activity: Philly Mag Dec 2024 and Visit Philly Aug 2026.

name: Carter's Cheesesteaks
tagline: Cheesesteaks from Garci Peterkin, Chinatown's first Black-owned business.
description: Garci Peterkin opened Carter's on Race Street in November 2025, becoming the first Black-owned business in Philadelphia's Chinatown. The menu centers on cheesesteaks.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Philadelphia Tribune and BuyBlack. Opened Nov 2025, Hoodline Feb 2026. Phone and website not confirmed.

name: Dahlak
tagline: Eritrean and Ethiopian food, a patio and live music on Baltimore Avenue.
description: Dahlak has served Eritrean and Ethiopian dishes on Baltimore Avenue since the 1980s. Family run, it doubles as a neighborhood hub with a patio, open mics, jazz and club nights.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly 2026 guide; family ownership per 34th Street (Oct 2024). Founding year differs between sources (1984 vs. 1986), left null.

name: African American Museum in Philadelphia
tagline: The first city-built museum for African American history, founded in 1976.
description: AAMP opened in 1976 as the first institution built by a major U.S. city to preserve and show African American history and culture. Its permanent exhibit covers Black Philadelphians from 1776 to 1876, and its 50th anniversary exhibition opens in fall 2026.

_verified.note: Black-founded institution per Visit Philly African American historic sites (updated Aug 10, 2026). Open: own site announces AAMP at 50 for fall 2026; galleries closed from Sept 7 for the exhibition changeover, so check before visiting.

name: The Colored Girls Museum
tagline: A Germantown house museum honoring the stories of Black girls and women.
description: Founded by Vashti DuBois, this museum in a Germantown Victorian house collects objects and art that tell the stories of Black girls and women. It marks its 10th anniversary in 2026 and offers weekend tours.

_verified.note: Black-founded (Vashti DuBois) per own site and Inquirer (July 20, 2026). Open: weekend tours on own site, 2026 coverage. Founding year not stated directly, left null.

name: Philadelphia Clef Club of Jazz & Performing Arts
tagline: South Broad jazz venue and school rooted in Philly's Black musicians' union.
description: The Clef Club grew out of AFM Local 274, the city's Black musicians' union, and was founded in 1966. It runs jazz education programs and concerts on South Broad Street and celebrates its 60th anniversary in 2026.

_verified.note: Black-founded per Visit Philly historic sites and HSP. Activity: 60th anniversary events June to Sept 2026. Its own about page returned an error, so website left null.

name: New Freedom Theatre
tagline: Pennsylvania's oldest Black theatre company, on North Broad since 1966.
description: Founded by John E. Allen Jr. in 1966, New Freedom Theatre is Pennsylvania's oldest Black theatrical organization. It runs performances and training programs from its North Broad Street home.

_verified.note: Black-founded per Visit Philly historic sites (Aug 2026). Draft because its site shows no dated 2025 or 2026 productions. Phone listed as 844-NFT-PHIL, left null as it does not fit the format.

name: Ubuntu Fine Art
tagline: Germantown photo gallery showing Steven CW Taylor's travel prints.
description: Photographer Steven CW Taylor shows his travel photography in this Germantown gallery, founded in 2021. Visits pair the prints with ambient sound and scent, and each print comes with a certificate of authenticity.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly Black-owned shops guide (updated July 28, 2026). Own site live with 2026 copyright and states founded 2021.

name: Urban Art Gallery
tagline: West Philly gallery giving emerging artists a first wall.
description: Kalphonse Morris runs this 52nd Street gallery where emerging artists show early work. It hosts exhibitions and community programs and sells art in person and online.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly Black-owned shops guide (July 2026). Own site live, current show page references a 2025 Caribbean Creatives show. Generic name, so slug includes city.

name: Hakim's Bookstore & Gift Shop
tagline: The oldest Black-owned bookstore on the East Coast, on 52nd Street since 1959.
description: Dawud Hakim opened this West Philly bookstore in 1959, and his daughter Yvonne Blake runs it today. It stocks books on Black history and culture and was named a Pennsylvania historic landmark in 2023.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly historic sites (Aug 10, 2026) and Wikipedia. Activity: listed in both 2026 Visit Philly guides and site is live. Phone not confirmed.

name: Harriett's Bookshop
tagline: Jeannine A. Cook's Fishtown bookstore celebrating women authors and activists.
description: Jeannine A. Cook opened Harriett's in Fishtown in February 2020, naming it for Harriet Tubman. It focuses on women authors, art and activism, and a second shop is listed at 921 Market Street.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026). Open: own site lists daily hours. Old harriettsbookshop.com now redirects to oursisterbookshops.com.

name: Uncle Bobbie's Coffee & Books
tagline: Germantown bookstore and coffee shop founded by Marc Lamont Hill.
description: Marc Lamont Hill opened Uncle Bobbie's on Germantown Avenue in 2017, naming it for his favorite uncle. It sells new releases, local authors and children's books alongside coffee, and hosts author events.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026). Open: live site with hours and events.

name: Blue Sole Shoes
tagline: Rittenhouse men's shoe boutique for Italian footwear since 2007.
description: Steve Jamison opened this Chestnut Street men's footwear shop in 2007. It carries Italian shoes, socks, accessories and apparel from designers like Magnanni and Harris.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026). Open: own site with 2026 copyright, address and phone.

name: Senoj Clothing
tagline: South Street women's boutique for dresses, bodysuits and outerwear.
description: Charrita Jones runs Senoj, a women's boutique on South Street. It sells dresses, bodysuits, skirts, outerwear, sunglasses and handbags in store and online.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026, owner Charrita Jones). Online shop live with 2026 copyright. ZIP and phone not confirmed.

name: Wash Day
tagline: Northern Liberties salon for curly and textured hair.
description: Tori McCutcheon and Ruth Mullen run Wash Day, a natural hair salon for curly and textured hair. Services include cuts, color, skincare, waxing and brow and lash work, booked online.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026). Own site live with online booking; address from Visit Philly since the site does not list one. Generic name, so slug includes city.

name: Duafe Holistic Hair Care
tagline: North Philly natural hair salon for locs, braids and twists.
description: Stylist Syreeta Scott runs this North Philly salon, known for locs, braids, two-strand twists and color. It also sells its own vegan hair care line.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026, owner Syreeta Scott). Open: own site with hours, phone and Vagaro booking. Founding year inconsistent on site, left null.

name: Dope Botanicals
tagline: Rittenhouse apothecary for herbs, teas, tonics and tinctures.
description: Sisters Nakia and Taahirah Stith run this plant-based apothecary near Rittenhouse Square. It sells herbs, teas, tonics, tinctures and smoothies.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026). Open: own site with hours and 2026 copyright.

name: Rise & Ritual
tagline: West Philly tea house and apothecary with workshops and tea ceremonies.
description: Taylor Nickens founded Rise & Ritual, a tea house and apothecary on North 52nd Street. It offers loose-leaf herbal teas, herbal foot baths, workshops and tea ceremonies.

_verified.note: Black-owned per own site and Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026). Draft because the site shows no dated 2025 or 2026 events, and its ZIP is a typo, so ZIP left null.

name: Mount Airy Candle Co.
tagline: Hand-poured soy candles and fragrances made in Mount Airy.
description: Marques Davis founded Mount Airy Candle Co. in 2018. It makes hand-poured soy candles and eau de parfum, sold online, at its studio and at shops around Pennsylvania.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026, founder Marques Davis, founded 2018). Open: own site with 2026 copyright and August 2026 content. ZIP not confirmed.

name: Plant & People
tagline: Mother and daughter plant shop with wellness goods and workshops.
description: Cherron Perry-Thomas and Amma Thomas run this plant shop, selling houseplants, fair trade wellness goods, books and handmade accessories. They also host plant swaps and community workshops.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly shops guide (July 2026). Own site (2026 copyright) lists 3952 Lancaster Ave while Visit Philly lists 1431 N 52nd St; the first-party address is used, confirm before publishing.

name: FarmerJawn
tagline: Christa Barfield's organic farm, CSA and farm store in Chester County.
description: Christa Barfield founded FarmerJawn, which grows chemical-free vegetables, herbs and fruit. It runs a produce CSA, a farm store and Viva Leaf Tea, with a Kensington shop in the works.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Black Farmers Index (West Chester and Philadelphia). Open: own site takes 2026 CSA signups. Street address not shown on the site, left null.

name: Sankofa Community Farm at Bartram's Garden
tagline: Southwest Philly farm growing crops of the African diaspora.
description: Sankofa Community Farm grows food at Bartram's Garden with a focus on crops and traditions of the African diaspora. In 2026 it runs farm stands at Bartram's, Clark Park and a Black farmers market, and accepts EBT and WIC farmers market vouchers.

_verified.note: Listed on Black Farmers Index. Founded 2011 per Bartram's farm page, which lists 2026 farm stand dates including Oct 15 and 17. It is a program of Bartram's Garden, a nonprofit; phone is Bartram's main line.

name: Mill Creek Urban Farm
tagline: West Philly urban farm with a Saturday farm stand at 49th and Brown.
description: Mill Creek Urban Farm has grown vegetables, fruit and herbs at 49th and Brown Streets since 2005. Its farm stand runs Saturdays and accepts Farmers Market Nutrition Program vouchers.

_verified.note: Listed on Black Farmers Index. Draft because the live site shows Saturday stand hours but no dated 2025 or 2026 activity.

name: Alif Brew & Mini Mart
tagline: Ethiopian cafe and corner store on Baltimore Avenue.
description: Sisters Hayat Ali and Mebruka Kane run Alif Brew, an Ethiopian cafe and corner store at 45th and Baltimore that opened in 2020. Stop in for coffee, chai, pantry staples and injera wraps.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Philly 2026 guide (owner Hayat Ali); owners and 2020 opening per 34th Street (Oct 2024). Mainly a cafe that also sells pantry staples; filed as grocery because no stronger grocery candidate was verified. alifbrew.com did not resolve.

name: United Bank of Philadelphia
tagline: Black-owned community bank founded by Emma C. Chappell in 1992.
description: Emma C. Chappell founded United Bank of Philadelphia in 1992 as a Black-owned commercial bank. It is a certified CDFI with a branch at Progress Plaza on North Broad Street.

_verified.note: FDIC record: active, MDI status Black or African American owned, established 03/23/1992, report date 06/30/2026. Branch address and phone from the bank's locations page (Progress Plaza).
